matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: When moving a matchstick, keep its original orientation (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal) to ensure the resulting symbols are valid.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick and placing it as a horizontal line, which changes the orientation and creates an invalid symbol.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick may be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick without placing it elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: For every solution, ensure only one stick is moved.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from a numeral and not placing it anywhere, effectively deleting a stick.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every symbol must still be a legal Roman numeral (I, V, X, L, C, D, M) or a valid operator (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each stick relocation, check each character.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to a V, resulting in a shape that is not a Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: Convert the Roman numerals on both sides of the equation to Arabic numbers and ensure the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a corrected equation, compute its numeric value to confirm correctness.
matchstick.example: Accepting an equation that looks syntactically valid but evaluates to 5 = 7.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V each consist of exactly two diagonal sticks; after moving a stick, each must still contain both diagonals, otherwise the symbol becomes invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a diagonal stick from X or V.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from an X, leaving a single diagonal line, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final response must end with a line exactly matching 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>'. Whitespace must be collapsed and case normalized.
matchstick.example: Writing 'Correct version of the equation:IV=XI-VII' without spaces, causing a format mismatch.

matchstick.title: Validate single‑stick relocation feasibility
matchstick.principle: After proposing a corrected equation, verify that the change can be achieved by moving exactly one stick (i.e., the source character can lose a stick and remain valid, and the target character can gain the stick and remain valid).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalizing a solution, simulate the stick move.
matchstick.example: Attempting to move a stick from a minus sign (which would delete it) without providing a replacement, leaving an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Do not break I
matchstick.principle: When moving the only stick from an I (a single vertical stick), the I character must be removed entirely; you cannot leave a half‑I.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a vertical stick from an isolated I.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from an I and leaving an empty space, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator stick transformation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from or to an operator (+, -, =), ensure the resulting operator is a valid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is moved to or from an operator.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to a minus sign, turning it into an invalid shape rather than a plus sign.

matchstick.title: Swap operators via horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If the equation contains both '=' and '-' (or '+'), moving a single horizontal stick from '=' to '-' (or vice versa) swaps the operators while preserving orientation; this often yields a correct equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is close to correct and includes both an equality sign and a subtraction (or addition) sign.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' but leaving '=' with only one horizontal line, which is not a valid '=' operator.

matchstick.title: Transfer vertical stick between I's
matchstick.principle: When adjusting values, moving a vertical stick from an isolated I (which disappears) to another numeral that can accept an extra I (e.g., I, II, III, IV, VI, VII) increases its value by 1 while keeping all symbols valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by a small amount and contains I's that can be transferred without breaking other numerals.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to a V, creating an invalid numeral, instead of adding it to a numeral that can accept an extra I.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may focus on visual validity of symbols and forget to check the numeric equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always convert the Roman numerals to Arabic numbers after any change and confirm the equality holds.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may output the corrected equation in a different line or with extra whitespace.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: End the response with exactly 'Correct version of the equation: <equation>' and collapse whitespace.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may remove a stick from a character without placing it elsewhere, violating the one‑stick‑move rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure every moved stick has a clear destination that results in a valid symbol.

matchstick.description: Breaking a numeral by moving a stick away, leaving an invalid shape (e.g., V with one diagonal, X with one diagonal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may not consider the structural integrity of multi‑stick symbols.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Apply the 'Do not break X or V' and 'Do not break I' rules before moving sticks.

matchstick.description: Creating invalid Roman numeral (e.g., IIII, invalid ordering)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may add sticks to a numeral in a way that violates Roman numeral syntax.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick addition, check that the resulting numeral follows standard Roman numeral rules.
